items.title: 1Password Hacked, Customer Data and Source Code Stolen in GitHub Account Breach
items.summary: Popular password management software 1Password on Wednesday disclosed a security incident involving its backend systems that led to the unauthorized access of some customer information, but emphasized that customer password vaults and other secrets were not accessed.

also_covered_by.title: 1Password says breach exposed customer details
also_covered_by.summary: 1Password says attackers who broke into its internal systems copied limited account details from some customers, but could not access password vaults or the secrets protecting them. The company detected the intrusion on November 19 and says customers do not need to reset passwords or change account settings. Source

also_covered_by.title: 1Password: Customer data stolen
also_covered_by.summary: Why hack the database when you can rewrite the backend? 1Password customer data fell into unauthorized hands. Watch out for phishing!

also_covered_by.title: 1Password Breach Exposes Customer Data, Internal Source Code
also_covered_by.summary: A hacker used a compromised employee GitHub account to push malicious code and steal customer records, but vaults were not accessed.

also_covered_by.title: 1Password breached through hijacked employee GitHub account, customer names and emails stolen
also_covered_by.summary: An attacker who got into a 1Password employee’s corporate GitHub account went on to copy account records for some of the company’s users and source code from private repositories, the password manager maker disclosed on Wednesday.
